# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark
# on a single-node (size: 1) Kubernetes cluster with AWS ARM CPU instances.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A unique name for the MiniCluster instance to avoid collisions.
  name: amg-test-1
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. For this test, we start with 1.
  size: 1
  # This section defines the container that runs the user's application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The application command to run. Flux will wrap this command for execution.
      # We run AMG, problem type 2, with a small 4x4x4 processor grid for initial testing.
      command: "amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4"
      # The main application container is not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Configuration for the Flux Framework itself.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture as ARM, required for ARM-based instances (e.g., AWS Graviton).
    arch: "arm"
    # Use the ARM-compatible version of the flux-view sidecar container.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines logging behavior for the MiniCluster.
  logging:
    # Fails the job if any non-zero exit codes are detected from flux services.
    strict: true

  # Set to false to keep the pods and associated resources after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest runs the AMG2023 benchmark,
# addressing the task-to-processor mismatch from the previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A new unique name for the MiniCluster instance to avoid collisions.
  name: amg-test-2
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods for the MiniCluster remains 1 for this test.
  size: 1
  # Set the total number of MPI tasks to 64 to match the processor grid (4*4*4).
  tasks: 64
  # Set to false to keep pods for debugging after the job completes.
  cleanup: false
  # This section defines the single application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command remains the same, but now the task count matches the processor grid.
      command: "amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4"
      # The main application container is not the launcher.
      launcher: false
      # Environment variables for performance tuning and EFA network configuration.
      environment:
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"
        FI_PROVIDER: "efa"
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_pml: "cm"
        OMPI_MCA_btl: "^openib"
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Configuration for the Flux Framework itself.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture as ARM for AWS Graviton instances.
    arch: "arm"
    # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view sidecar container.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
    # Flux option flag to ensure each task is bound to a specific CPU core.
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"

  # Defines logging behavior for the MiniCluster.
  logging:
    # Fails the job if any non-zero exit codes are detected from flux services.
    strict: true
